issues.current_text: Trump pausou a operação de escolta de navios retidos no Estreito de Ormuz para abrir espaço a um acordo com o Irã, enquanto Estados Unidos e aliados do Golfo propuseram uma nova resolução no Conselho de Segurança da ONU... Cerca de 22.500 tripulantes em mais de 1.550 navios comerciais permanecem retidos no Golfo.
issues.previous_text: Forças americanas reabriram uma faixa do Estreito de Ormuz após afundar seis embarcações iranianas que miravam navios civis. Na mesma segunda-feira, o Irã disparou 15 mísseis e 4 drones contra os Emirados Árabes Unidos.
issues.suggestion: Running story with genuine new developments (pause in escorts, UN resolution, crew count). Acceptable as continuation, but open with the new pivot (Trump pausing escorts) rather than re-setting the scene. The reader already knows about the Strait crisis — lead with what changed.

issues.current_text: a presidente da Comissão Europeia, Ursula von der Leyen, respondeu à ameaça de Trump de elevar tarifas sobre carros europeus para 25% lembrando que o acordo de Turnberry já fixava a alíquota em 15%, e Macron endossou retaliação.
issues.previous_text: os EUA confirmaram elevação de tarifas sobre carros europeus a 25%, rompendo o acordo comercial de 2025. Ministros de finanças da UE disseram que todas as opções de retaliação estão na mesa.
issues.suggestion: The 25% tariff on EU cars and EU retaliation were already covered yesterday. Today's new angle is von der Leyen invoking the Turnberry deal and Macron specifically endorsing retaliation. Rewrite to foreground the new (von der Leyen's legal/diplomatic argument, Macron's position) and drop the 25% re-explanation — the reader saw it yesterday.

issues.previous_text: [May 5] Anthropic's Mythos model triggered White House AI vetting discussion. [May 4] A Anthropic está finalizando uma joint venture de US$1,5 bilhão com a Blackstone, o Goldman Sachs... Anthropic abriu o beta público do Claude Security.
issues.suggestion: Anthropic appears in 2+ stories in each of the last 3 editions (6+ mentions in 3 days). Each story is genuinely different, but the cumulative effect risks making the newsletter feel like an Anthropic tracker. Consider consolidating today's two Anthropic items into one sentence or dropping the less impactful one (finance agents catalog vs. $200B cloud commitment — the cloud deal is bigger news).

issues.suggestion: The '[Company], [nationality] [descriptor]' appositive clause is the default template for introducing every company. Today's draft has at least 5 instances. Vary the structure: lead with what the company did, put the descriptor in a subordinate clause, or skip it entirely for well-known names (AMD, Google, Meta don't need introductions).

issues.current_text: Semicondutores section leads the newsletter with blockbuster market cap / revenue numbers, followed by Balanços with more chip-related earnings.
issues.previous_text: Semicondutores section leads May 5 (global sales heading to $1T) and May 4 (Nvidia China sales at zero, EU gigafactories).
issues.suggestion: Semiconductors have led or dominated 3 consecutive editions. Today's edition doubles down with both a 'Semicondutores' and a 'Balanços' section that is also mostly chip companies (AMD, Infineon, Super Micro). Consider merging them or leading with a different section (Agentes or Infraestrutura are both strong today) to break the pattern.

issues.current_text: Geopolítica section closes the newsletter with Iran + EU trade items bundled together.
issues.previous_text: Geopolítica section closes May 5 with Iran + EU tariffs + China anti-sanctions bundled together. May 4 closes with energy/OPEC.
issues.suggestion: Iran-Strait-of-Hormuz + US-EU tariffs have appeared as a closing geopolitics bundle for 2 consecutive days. The reader may start skimming. If both stories stay, consider splitting them: Iran/Gulf with infrastructure (energy implications) and EU tariffs with the semiconductor/trade section, since tariffs are fundamentally a tech supply chain story.

summary: Moderate repetition. Running geopolitical stories (Iran, EU tariffs) carry over with new developments but re-explain context the reader already has. Anthropic saturation across 3 editions. Structural monotony: semiconductors always lead, geopolitics always closes, company introductions follow a rigid template.
